newsitem.title: UK: Brokers say few redemptions from DMG funds.
newsitem.headline: Brokers say few redemptions from DMG funds.

text.p: UK brokers said they have had few redemptions in the three Morgan Grenfell funds which resumed trading on Thursday after being suspended pending investigations into unquoted holdings.

Trade in MG European Growth trust, MG Europa Fund and MG European Capital Growth fund was suspended on Monday, and the manager of the European Growth and the European Capital Growth, Peter Young, was suspended.
Now Morgan Grenfell Asset Management has suspended Stewart Armer, manager of the MG Europa fund on a suspected breach of personal account dealing rules.

But brokers handling enquiries from independent financial advisers (IFAs), who control millions of pounds worth of business through their retail clients, said there had been no rush to sell holdings in the Morgan Grenfell funds.
Janice Thompson at Chelsea Financial Services in London said they had only had one redemption this morning.

"It hasn't been that frantic. We have only done one redemption and a couple of people have asked us not to place deals they had previously lined up. There have been one or two PEP (personal equity plan) transfers."

"Our advice is not to sell and let things calm down," she added. "We hold a lot in discretionary accounts -- up to 400,000 pounds. We are not selling that, we are all holders ourselves and we are not selling."
Another major broker who declined to be named said there had been many enquiries but no redemptions.

"It is not that amazing...most are comforted by Deutsche Bank standing behind it. We are quite happy because it looks like they have got rid of any marginal quality assets and there is plenty of cash for a clean start with a new fund manager."
He added that the funds would be under intense scrutiny from now on.
A broker based in the Midlands said Morgan Grenfell was widely considered to have done a good job "picking up on managers who have overstepped the mark."
"It has been embarassing for them to be in the papers but the clients have not done badly because Deutsche Bank have picked up the tab."
However, most brokers noted that it was unlikely that IFAs would have contacted their clients within a day of the funds resuming trading.
"It will take them a few weeks to get back to customers and discuss it all, get instructions and then move. Look again at these funds in the next three months."
